newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan traders unruffled by Russia Almaz news.
newsitem.headline: Japan traders unruffled by Russia Almaz news.

text.p: Japanese traders said on Tuesday that reaction was muted to news that Russia expects its exports of platinum group metals to Japan to fall this year, as the market had already discounted such a possibility.

The agency handling Russia's exports of platinum group metals, Almazjuvelirexport (Almaz), said on Monday that its exports to Japan would be much lower this year than in 1996 and no palladium would be exported to Japan in March.
Traders said problems with the palladium shipments had been clear for some time so they had already been taken into account.

"The statement hardly came as a surprise as we have already given up on shipments of platinum group metals in March," a trader at a major trading house said, adding that there was a growing possibility that there would be no shipments in April as well.
"We were disappointed with the remarks, as there was no progress in the deadlocked Japan-Russia talks on platinum group metals," another trading house trader said.
The statement was issued in Japan on Monday by a Russian trade representative.

Russian palladium shipments to Japan have been on hold since the beginning of the year due to delays in 1997 supply contract talks. The two countries usually hold export talks in the middle of December but they have been postponed due to Russian budget problems and government changes.
Japanese traders are unhappy about buying in the spot market to cover their requirements due to rising prices, but they have no choice but to do so, they said.
They added that spot palladium prices are unlikely to slip from the current levels unless there is a clear resumption of Russian exports.
Supplies of palladium sponge, a form of the metal used in cars' catalytic converters, are still extremely tight, they said.
Lease rates of palladium have been rising, reflecting the tightness in the physical market, the traders said.
